Except for the procurement of janitorial and custodial supplies for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, which shall be the responsibility of the University, the Manager is author ized to purchase all materials, equipment, tools, appliances, supplies and services necessary to assure proper maintenance and repair of the Student Housing Facilities subject to the limits of the Annual Budget, and all of such costs shall be Program Expenses.
The Manager’s maintenance and repair obligations shall include, but are not limited to, maintenance and operation of the HVAC equipment, elevator system s, and other mechanical equipment and operation systems serving the Student Housing Facilities, and al l other necessary maintenance of and repairs to the Student Housing Facilities to the extent funds are made available pursuant to the Annual Budget; provided, however, the Manager shall not be responsible for any custodial services at the New Undergraduate Housing Projects.
Lessee shall cause the University to be responsible for all landscaping and snow removal of the Student Housing Facilities.

The Manager shall not be responsible for any landscaping of the Student Housing Facilities, but will cause the University to be reimbursed as a Program Expense for any expenses incurred by the University for such landscaping, provided such expenses are within the Annual Budget.
The Manager shall not be responsible for any snow removal of the Student Housing Facilities, but will cause the University to be reimbursed as a Program Expense for any expenses incurred by the University for such snow removal from the areas between the line th at is twenty feet from the exterior doors of the Student Housing Facilities to the adjacent parking areas, as more particularly detailed in the Affiliation Agreement and the Responsibility Matrix, provided such expenses are within the Annual Budget.
The Manager shall not have any responsibility for the maintenance of any exterior signs adjacent to any of the Student Housing Facilities, but will maintain signs affixed to the Student Housing Facilities, subject to the approval of the University, provided all costs incurred for such maintenance of signs affixed to the Student Housing Facilities is a Program Expense and is refl ected in the Annual Budget.

The Manager shall not have any responsibility for the maintenance, lighting, snow removal or cleaning of any parking lots and the costs thereof shall not be a Program Expense.
Section 3.2 Work Order Management.
The Manager shall track and document work orders using an electronic system to manage work orders that is selected and implemented by the Manager, or with the consent of the Lessee, implemented by the Lessee.
Information gathered through the use of the work order system will be used to assist in monitoring and maintaining the Student Housing Facilities, and the work order system will assist the Manager in tracking preventative maintenance and annual inspections to determine the condition of the Student Housing Facilities.
The work order system shall have an online user interface that will allow online submission of requests by Residents and residence life staff, provide notifications of work orders to the Manager, and provide the Lessee and the University with access to status reports and dashboards.
The work order system shall also track the amount of time occurring between work order submission and work order completion.

Provided work order completion for any work order submission has not occurred within a reasonable amount of time after such work order submission and after at least thirty (30) days advance written notice by the University to the Manager and the Lessee of such failure to complete in a reasonable amount of time, the University or the Lessee may complete the work in such work order submission; provided, however, if the work in such work order submission has commenced

7 4923-6384-1828.6 within such thirty (30) day period and is proceeding in a reasonable manner, then the University and the Lessee shall not have the right to complete such work.
Section 3.3 Use of Maintenance Employees .
The Manager will utilize the services of its regular maintenance employees to maintain and repair the Student Housing Facilities except in circumstances where the Manager determines that use of such employees for a given task would be an unproductive use of their time, where the Manager determines that the use of a third party vendor or contractor would likely yield superior results than the use of its regular employees, or when such employees are otherwise occupied or unavailable; provided, however, the use of such third party vendors or contractors shall not increase the expenses set forth in Annual Budget without Lessee’s approval (and the approval of the University, if required by the Ground Lease).
Section 3.4 Preventative Maintenance .

The Manager shall develop and implement preventative maintenance and scheduled service plans (“Preventative Maintenance Plans”) for all capital equipment of the Student Housing Facilities, which Preventative Maintenance Plans shall be presented to and subject to the approval of, the University as part of the process of determining the Annual Budget each Annual Period.
The Manager shall schedule and perform preventative maintenance on the Student Housing Facilities consistent with good maintenance and repair practices, and in accordance with the Preventative Maintenance Plan, subject to limitations contained in the Annual Budget.
Section 3.5 Damage by Residents The Manager shall assess and determine any and all damages to a Student Housing Facility beyond reasonab le wear and tear caused by any Resident or such Resident’s guests.

Based on such assessment and determination of damages by the Manager, the Lessee shall cause the University to invoice any such Resident in a New Undergraduate Housing Project and the Manager will invoice any such Resident in the Graduate Housing Project for the costs to repair any such damage for which such Resident is responsible in accordance with a damages and billing sheet, the form of which has been mutually agreed upon by the Manager, Lessee and University.
Section 3.6 Capital Improvements and Work .
The Lessee, and not the Manager, will be primarily responsible for causing the completion of the construction of the Student Housing Facilities pursuant to the Development Agreement.
With respect to each Student Housing Facility, if Lessee is permitted, pursuant to Section 13.2 of the Ground Lease, to make additional capital improvements to the Property applicable to such Student Housing Facility after the Effective Date for such Student Housing Facility, the Manager shall include all such planned capital improvements in its proposed Annual Budget.

The Manager shall develop a capital improvement plan for the first ten (10) years of the Term detailing capital improvements that will be needed to the Student Housing Facilities during such period of time (“Capital Improvement Plan”), which Capital Improvement Plan shall be presented to and subject to the approval of the University as part of the process of determining the Annual Budget each Annual Period.
The Manager, consistent with the Capital Improvement Plan shall be responsible for planning, designing, managing, implementing and constructing major and minor capital improvements at the Student Housing Facilities and/or supervising third-party construction agents responsible for managing any such capital improvements at the Student Housing Facilities.

In connection with such work, the Manager shall be responsible for (a) preparing and reviewing all draw requests for submission to the Lessee and, if requested by Lessee, pay all draw requests on approval by Lessee; (b) requiring each contractor and subcontractor to maintain insurance as required by the Transaction Documents or such greater coverages as are required by the Lessee; and (c) soliciting competitive bids from such contractors when required by Applicable Law or when the cost of a capital improvement exceeds $50,000.
Prior to undertaking any work or responsibilities which Manager believes are not already obligations of the Manager pursuant to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Manager shall submit to Lessee a proposal with sufficient detail that outlines such additional work or responsibilities, why the Manager believes such additional work or responsibilities are not contemplated by this Agreement, the anticipated labor and overhead costs to be incurred by the Manager

8 4923-6384-1828.6 in order to perform such additional work or responsib ilities, and any additional fees or charges proposed for such work (such costs, fees and charges, collectively the “ Capital Improvement Fee ”).
If such additional work or responsibilities and the related costs are approved by the Lessee, the Manager shall be compensated the Capital Improvement Fee for such additional work or responsibilities (as a Program Expense), which shall be in addition to the Base Management Fee and Property Management Performance Incentive Fee.
Section 3.7 Ownership of Personal Property .
The Lessee shall own all Personalty located in the Student Housing Facilities as of the Effective Date, other than property of Residents or other third parties, but the Manager, on behalf of the Lessee, has the right to use, maintain, repair, and dispose of all of such personal property in connection with the discharge of its rights and obligations hereunder.

Any such personal property and any other personal property hereinafter acquired by the Lessee, or the Manager on behalf of the Lessee, for use in connection with the Student Housing Facilities shall be conveyed to the University at the expiration or earlier termination of the Ground Lease, if so provided in the Ground Lease.
Section 3.8 Recycling and Waste Hauling.
Residents will be responsible for taking trash and items to be recycled from their units to designated trash areas for the Student Housing Facilities containing separate trash and recycling bins.
The Lessee will cause the University to remove trash and items to be recycled in the common areas of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to such designated trash areas for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and the Manager will remove trash and items to be recycled in the common areas of the Graduate Housing Project to such designated trash areas for the Graduate Housing Project.

The Lessee will cause the University to arrange for the pickup of such trash and recycling from all of such designated trash areas for all of the Student Housing Facilities pursuant to contracts between the University and third party contractors, which expenses shall be Program Expenses to be reflected on the Annual Budget and reimbursed to the University per the Annual Budget.
Section 3.9 Janitorial Services.
Lessee shall cause the University to provide all janitorial and custodial services to all of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and such services shall be maintained at a level of 1 to 2.9 under the APPA standards.
The Manager will provide all janitorial and custodial services for the Graduate Housing Project.
ARTICLE IV SERVICE CONTRACTS Section 4.1 Generally.

The Manager shall enter into new service contracts for the Student Housing Facilities (each, a “Service Contract,” and collectively, “Service Contracts”), in its own name or as agent and attorney-in-fact of the Lessee, in th e ordinary course of its management of the Student Housing Facilities; provided, however, notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Article IV, no such Service Contracts shall be with any vendor on the University’s list of Excluded Vendors (“ Excluded Vendor”), provided such exclusion is permitted by Applicable Law.
Except in emergency situations where it is infeasible for the Manager to consult with the Un iversity’s Office of Strategic Procurement prior to engaging a vendor, Manager shall contact the University’s Office of Strategic Procurement to enquire as to the whether a potential vendor is an Excluded Vendor.
Service Contracts may govern, without limitation, the procurement of goods and services (including utilities and maintenance services) for the Student Housing Facilities and the furnishing of goods and services to Residents of the Student Housing Facilities.

All costs and expenses incurred by the Manager under the Service Contracts shall be Program Expenses.
The Manager shall keep good books and records of account relating to all Service Contracts.
The costs of any such good or service will be included and specifically identified as third party good or services in the Annual Budget.
Further, the Manager covenants that (i) all such contracts will satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-13 or any successor federal guidance and (ii) no such contracts will, when taken together with this Agreement, cause this Agreement not to satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-

9 4923-6384-1828.6 13 or any successor federal guidance.
The Manager shall maintain records for products and/or services delivered to the Manager and pursuant to this Agreement for a period commencing on the Effective Date and ending the later of the date that is (i) six (6) years after expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement and (ii) the date the books and records are required to be retained under the regulations and rulings promulgated under the Internal Revenue Code.
Section 4.2 Utilities and Services.
To the extent the University has not elected to provide the services described in this Section, the Manager, on behalf of the Lessee, shall enter into Service Contracts for the provision of water, electricity, gas, and other utilities for the Student Housing Facilities, as well as pest control and extermination services for the Student Housing Facilities, utilizing such utility companies and vendors as the Manager selects in its discretion.

Electricity and any other utilities serving the Student Housing Facilities, which are provided directly or indirectly by the University or which serve more than just the Student Housing Facilities, will be sub-metered for the Student Housing Facilities.
Water usage at the Student Housing Facilities shall be sub-metered and billed to the Manager by the University, and the Manager will pay such water charges billed by the University as a Program Expense.
Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement, electricity at the Student Housing Facilities will be sub-metered and billed to the Manager and the Manager will pay such electricity charges as a Program Expense.
Section 4.3 Bidding Requirements.

Unless the Lessee shall instruct otherwise, the Manager shall use reasonable efforts to ensure that all Service Contracts for the performance of repairs or capital improvements to any Student Housing Facility exceeding $50,000, or for the provision of goods and services to any Student Housing Facility exceeding $30,000, shall be awarded on the basis of a competitive bidding process managed by the Manager and approved by the Lessee; provided, however, no such Service Contract shall be awarded to an Excluded Vendor provided such exclusion is permitted by Applicable Law.
The Lessee's approval of the Annual Budget for the Student Housing Facilities shall be deemed approval for the work to be completed by Manager which is included in such Annual Budget.
Section 4.4 Term of Service Contracts .
To the extent reasonably possible under the circumstances, all Service Contracts shall contain a provision permitting Manager or Lessee to terminate them, with or without cause and without penalty or premium, with a thirty (30) day notice, or sooner if the Manager or the Lessee is no longer involved with a Student Housing Facility for which such Service Contract relates.

Under no circumstances shall a Service Contract exceed the Term without the consent of the Lessee.
The Lessee shall have the right to waive this requirement in its discretion.
Section 4.5 Service Contracts with Affiliates .
Subject to any restrictions contained in the Transaction Documents, the Manager shall have the ri ght to contract with or otherwise deal with any Affiliate of the Manager for the sale of goods or services to it or to the Lessee, but only if the fees, terms and conditions for the provision of such goods or services are conspicuously disclosed in the Annual Budget and are at least as favorable to the Lessee or the Stud ent Housing Facilities as would be obtainable in an arm’s length transaction.
The costs of any such good or service will be included and specifically identified as third party good or services in the Annual Budget .
Further, the Manager covenants that (i) all such contracts will satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-13 or any successor federal guidance and (ii) no such contracts will, when taken together with this Agreement, cause this Agreement not to satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-13 or any successor federal guidance.

Section 4.6 Ancillary Concessions.
Except as otherwise provided the Responsibility Matrix, the Manager shall not be responsible and the Lessee shall cause the University to be responsible for or to cause the University to retain a third party responsible for, operating, managing, repairing and replacing the laundry facilities, vending machines, the Grab and Go Deli and similar ancillary concessions located at the Student Housing Facilities during the Term, and the costs thereof shall be the responsibility of the University and the revenues generated therefrom may be retained by the University and shall not be General

10 4923-6384-1828.6 Revenues; provided, however, the Manager shall be responsible for managing, repairing and replacing the laundry equipment at the Graduate Housing Project.
With respect to the Grab and Go Deli, the University will be charged a monthly fee for electricity based on a rate which will be the product of: i) the total electric bill for the electrical meter which measures electricity usage at the space occupied by the Grab and Go Deli plus all other space whose electricity usage is being measured by such electrical meter; and ii) the percentage of the square footage of the space occupied by the Grab and Go Deli as compared to the square footage of the total space in the Student Housing Facility that has electricity being measured by the same electrical meter.
For example, if the Grab and Go Deli is 1,000 square feet and 5,000 square feet of space in Student Housing Facility where the Grab and Go Deli is located and including the Grab and Go Deli space has electricity being measured by the same electrical meter, then the University will pay 20% of the electrical bill related to such electrical meter each month.

The Lessee shall cause the University to pay to the Manager all of such monthly fees for electricity at the Grab and Go Deli and such fees shall be included in the General Revenues.
ARTICLE V BUDGETING AND REPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES Section 5.1 Determination of Resident Housing Rates and Other Gross Fees .
The Manager, in consultation with the University, shall review and analyze market demand for the occupancy of the Student Housing Facilities and shall recommend to the Lessee the Resident Housing Rates and other Gross Fees to be charged to Residents each year.
The Lessee shall have the right to make the final decision as to the Resident Housing Rates and Gross Fees.

Section 5.2 Annual Budget. (a) The Manager, shall in consultation with Lessee and in accordance with Section 18 of the Ground Lease, develop in good faith, in its discretion and after consultation with the University, housing rates and other revenue services and a line-item operation and capital budget for the Student Housing Facilities for each Annual Period (collectively, the “Annual Budgets” and each, an “Annual Budget”) which provides for the payment of all Program Expenses and sets forth among other matters usually contained in budgets of similar nature, all information required under the Bond Documents.
Each Annual Budget shall be subject to the review and final approval of the Board of Managers.
The Annual Budget for the first Annual Period in which the Student Housing Facilities are completed has been approved by the Lessee and the University and is attached to the Ground Lease. (b) For the first Annual Period in which the Student Housing Facilities are completed, Manager shall submit a partial year budget to Lessee or the Committee, on behalf of the Lessee, no later than sixty (60) days prior to the initial occupancy of the Student Housing Facilities.

Commencing with the second Annual Period and for each Annual Period thereafter, the Manager shall submit to the Lessee or the Committee, on behalf of the Lessee, for its approval a proposed Annual Budget not later than one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the commencement of each Annual Period.
The Committee shall give Lessee notice of its approval of the Annual Budget as submitted or of its disapproval of one or more of the matters contained therein not later than thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of the first Annual Period with respect to the initial partial year and sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of such Annual Pe riod thereafter.
If the Committee shall fail to give notice of approval or disapproval in a timely manner, then the Annual Budget as submitted to the Committee shall be deemed approved by the Committee and submitted for final approval to the Board of Managers.
In the event the Committee gives notice of its disapproval, the Committee shall promptly, in good faith, develop an Annual Budget on which the Committee can recommend to the Board of Managers for approval.
In the event Committee fails to reach agreement not later

11 4923-6384-1828.6 than thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of an Annual Period, or the Board of Managers fails to approve an Annual Budget submitted to them, the approved Annual Budget for the then current Annual Period, as increased by a factor equal to the Consumer Price Index Increase shall be implemented for the next Annual Period until a new Annual Budget is approved by Board of Managers. (c) From time to time during or in respect to an Annual Period, an Annual Budget may be modified pursuant to Section 18.3 of the Ground Lease.
The Manager may submit to Lessee proposed changes or other modifications to the Annual Budget and the Lessee shall seek in good faith to obtain such changes or modifications to the Annual Budget subject to Section 18.3 of the Ground Lease. (d) Subject to the limitations and restrictions se t forth in this Agreement, the Manager, on behalf of the Lessee, shall operate the Student Housing Facilities and make expenditures in connection with the Student Housing Facilities in accordance with the Annual Budget, and shall provide quarterly budget reconciliations to Lessee.
Section 5.3 Program Expenses.

All costs paid or incurred by the Manager in connection with the exercise of its rights or the discharge of its responsibilities under this Agreement including, but not limited to, all Operating Expenses shall be Program Expenses (“ Program Expenses ”); provided that Program Expenses shall not include corporate overhead costs of the Manager (including allocated costs of offsite employees) or any other cost or expenses unless such corporate overhead costs or other costs or expenses are approved in the Annual Budget.
Program Expenses shall be payable solely from the Operating Account and shall not be a personal obligation of the Manager.
Manager shall not be liable for any obligation or expenditure incurred on behalf of the Lessee if such obligation or expenditure is within the scope of Manager’s authority under this Agreement and pursuant to the Annual Budget (as the same may from time to time be amended and approved by Lessee).

Manager shall not be obligated to advance any sum of money for Lessee or the Student Housing Facilities, or lend its credit for the benefit of the Lessee or Student Housing Facilities; provided, however, if Manager elects to advance sums of money to pay for an Emergency Program Expense (as defined below) which funds are not available in the Operating Account or are not reflected in the Annual Budget, then the Annual Budget sh all be amended to reflect such Emergency Program Expense and Manager shall be reimbursed for such Emergency Program Expense within thirty (30) days of Manager incurring such Emergency Program Expense.
Manager shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the actual costs of maintaining and operating the Projects shall not exceed the Annual Budget, and year to date budget variances, in excess of (i) $20,000 for any line item expense category, excluding insurance and utility costs, or (ii) 10% of the Annual Budget in the aggregate, will be explained to Lessee each month.

Except as otherwise set forth herein or except for any Emergency Program Expense, any expenditure from the Operating Account (i) which, with respect to any line item expense category, exceeds by $20,000 or more the amount for such line item expense category set forth in the Annual Budget, or (ii) which will cause the overall Annual Budget to be exceeded by 10% or more, shall require the approval of Lessee, which approval shall be given or denied within ten (10) days after such approval is requested.
In cases of an emergency, Manager may make expenditures for repairs or replacements without the approval of Lessee or the University, if it is necessary, in the reasonable judgment of Manager, to prevent imminent damage to property or injury to persons and such expenditures shall be a Program Expense (“Emergency Program Expense”).
Manager will promptly notify Lessee and the University of any such emergency expenditures no later than two (2) Business Days following such emergency repair or replacement, describing the cause of such emergency, the repairs or replacements undertaken in connection with such emergency, and the cost of such emergency repairs or replacements.

12 4923-6384-1828.6 Section 5.4 Reports.
Unless otherwise directed by the Lessee, the Manager shall prepare (or coordinate the preparation of) all reports that the Less ee is obligated to provide to the University or any other Person under the Transaction Documents, a preliminary list of which is attached hereto in Schedule 5.4.
The Manager shall submit drafts of all such reports to the Lessee, for the Lessee’s review and approval, before submission to any Person other than the Lessee.
All records related to the operations of the Student Housing Facilities that are under the control of the Manager, regardless of where they are housed, shall be the property of Lessee and shall be properly maintained by or under the direction of the Manager.
The Manager shall also prepare and submit to the Lessee such additional reports as are reasonably requested by Lessee on a mutually acceptable schedule, and shall furnish such information as may be requested by the Lessee from time to time with respect to any matter falling within the scope of the Manager’s responsibilities herein.
Section 5.5 Notice of Material Events.

The Manager will immediately notify the Lessee in the following circumstances: (a) the Manager receives any notice of any claim of violation of any Applicable Laws relating to the Student Housing Facilities, any notice of any claim of liability or for damages relating to the Student Housing Facilities, or any summons or other legal process relating to the Student Housing Facilities; (b) any actual or alleged personal injury or property damage arises at the Student Housing Facilities; (c) circumstances arise relating to the activities of the Manager that will or may constitute a default by Lessee or any other Person under the Transaction Documents or under any Housing Agreement or Service Contract; (d) the Manager receives any information pertaining to the Lessee or the Student Housing Facilities, that requires Lessee to provide notice to the University under the Ground Lease, or that constitutes a breach by either the Lessee or the University under the Ground Lease; or (e) the Manager receives any other material information pertaining to its activities at the Student Housing Facilities.

The Manager will fully cooperate with the Lessee in all legal and arbitration proceedings relating to the Student Housing Facilities.
ARTICLE VI COLLECTIONS RESPONSIBILITIES Section 6.1 Generally.
With respect to the Graduate Housing Project, the Manager shall use diligent efforts to demand, collect and receive (a) all Gross Fees due and payable from Residents of the Graduate Housing Project, (b) all other pass-through or bill-back charges, sums, costs or expenses of any nature whatsoever payable by third parties relating to all or any portion of the Graduate Housing Project, and (c) all other General Revenues accruing from occupancy or use of, activities at, or services provided for Residents at the Graduate Housing Project.
The Manager shall abide by the collections procedures set forth in this Section.

Until all obligations of Lessee under the Bond Documents are paid in full, all General Revenues collected by Manager in the form of cash, checks or negotiable instruments shall be promptly deposited into a “deposit only” account owned by the Lessee (the “ Manager’s Collections Account”), which General Revenues in the Manager’s Collections Account shall be swept weekly from such Manager’s Collections Account for deposit into the Revenue Fund in accordance with Section 3.3 of the Loan and Trust Agreement and then an amount equal to the greater of the following will be transferred into the Operating Account on or before the 15th day of each month, all as set forth in Section 3.3 of the Loan and Trust Agreement: (i) the amount budgeted for Program Expenses in the Annual Budget for the immediately succeeding month; and (ii) an amount equal to ten percent (10%) of the Program Expenses shown in the then current Annual Budget.
From and after the da te that all obligations of Lessee under the Bond Documents are paid in full, all General Revenues collected by Manager in the form of cash, checks or negotiable instruments shall be directly deposited into the Operating Account.

All costs and expenses of the Manager incurred in connection with its collections efforts shall be Program Expenses.
Section 6.2 Collections Accounting Obligations .
The Manager will establish a cash management software system to identify and effectuate the transfer of General Revenues to the Manager’s

13 4923-6384-1828.6 Collections Account and maintain such system or a si milar system in place for the Term to ensure that General Revenues are identified and transferred appropriately after the receipt thereof in accordance with the terms of the Transaction Documents.
With resp ect to the Graduate Housing Project, Manager shall reconcile occupancy by Residents of the Graduate Housing Project to the actual General Revenues from such Residents, manage the accounts receivables, and collect delinquent revenues.
The Manager shall keep accurate books and records of account tracking the sources and uses of all funds and rent rolls for Residents of the Student Housing Facilities, and shall, to the extent possible, provide electronic copies of such books and records to the Lessee and the University as reasonably requested from time to time; provided, however, Lessee shall cooperate and shall cause the University to cooperate with providing any and all information related to the sources and uses of all funds and re nt rolls for Residents of the Undergraduate Housing Projects.

The Manager shall hold for a period of at least seven (7) years the Manager’s books and records that (i) evidence or relate to such General Revenues or (ii) are otherwise necessary or desirable to collect such General Revenues to the fullest extent allowed under Applicable Laws.
Section 6.3 Enforcement of Rights .
Without limitation of the foregoing and subject to the terms of the Ground Lease, the Manager shall have the right, on behalf of the Lessee and as a Program Expense, subject to the Annual Budget, to retain legal counsel to assist with the foregoing and/or to institute legal proceedings for: (a) the collection of General Revenues and other sums payable by Residents or other Persons under the terms of any of the Housing Agreements, Service Contracts, or other agreements affecting the Student Housing Facilities; (b) the ouster, eviction, removal or ejectment of Residents or other persons from the Student Housing Facilities, subject to Section 2.6 above; and (c) the enforcement of any other right, privilege, benefit, or remedy available to the Lessee pursuant to any of the Housing Agreements, the Service Contracts, or Applicable Laws.

ARTICLE VII CASH MANAGEMENT Section 7.1 Operating Account.
All funds paid to the Manager pursuant to Section 3.3(b) of the Loan and Trust Agreement, other than compensation to Manager under Article X of this Agreement, shall be promptly deposited into the Operating Account.
In addition to the Operating Account, the Manager may also use purchasing cards for miscellaneous purposes, which purchasing cards shall in no event exceed Five Thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($5,000.00).
The Manager shall maintain a ledger of Program Expenses funded from such purchasing cards.
Section 7.2 Funding the Operating Account .
The Lessee will from time to time fund the Operating Account from which the Manager shall have the right to make periodic withdrawals solely for the purpose of paying Program Expenses in accordance with the Annual Budget.
To the extent funds are available in the Operating Account, the Manager shall pay, using the funds in the Operating Account, the Program Expenses in accordance with the Annual Budget.
Section 7.3 Other Cash Management Provisions.

The Manager shall not commingle funds from the Student Housing Facilities with funds from any other project, other funds of the Manager, or funds of any other Person.
The Manager shall have no liability to the Lessee for any amounts in the Operating Account which are lost or not covered by insurance if the depository institution at which such account is maintained fails or is otherwise placed in the control of a governmental or quasi-governmental authority and the assets of such account are thereby forfeited in whole or in part.
The Manager shall not be obligated to make any advance to or for the account of the Lessee, or to pay any sum, except out of funds held or provided as set for in this Agreement.
The Lessee shall have the right to conduct audits of all accounts managed by the Manager, and the costs thereof shall be Program Expenses.

14 4923-6384-1828.6 ARTICLE VIII OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES OF MANAGER Section 8.1 Property Management Office .
The Manager may establish and maintain a housing management office and a maintenance office within one of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and also within the Graduate Housing Projec t.
All costs of furnishing and maintaining supplies for the management and maintenance offices shall be Program Expenses.
The Lessee shall not charge and shall cause the University to not charge the Manager any rent or other usage fees for the use of the housing management and maintenance offices, but if the University provides any services to such offices, such as telephone or internet access, the University shall be entitled to reimbursement therefor as Program Expenses at rates consistent with those assessed by the University to its own internal divisions and business units for similar services.

In the event the Manager becomes obligated to pay any rent, usage fees or charges for services provided to any office used by the Manager for providing property management services for the Student Housing Facilities, then such rent, usage fees or charges shall be Program Expenses to the extent included in the Annual Budget.
Section 8.2 Security and Emergency Response.
The Manager shall not have any responsibility for providing campus police or any on-site security not providing services and any such services or staffing shall be the responsibility of the Lessee or the Lessee shall cause the University to provide such campus police, services or staffing.
The Manager shall coordinate with the Lessee, and the University, any responses prior to (if reasonably possible), during and after potential disasters, conflicts or emergency situations, to minimize the risk of loss of life or property.
The Manager, in collaboration with the University, shall develop a continuity of operations plan to be utilized in the event of an emergency.
Such plan shall be reviewed and approved by the Committee annually.

Such plan will include plans for relocation of Residents for emergency or temporary housing, adequate on-call services to minimize and protect assets from actual or potential damage, and an emergency notification plan for all of the Manager’s personnel and all of the University’s personnel responsible for the same under this Agreement.
The Manager shall coordinate with the University to esta blish emergency points of contact from time to time, or pursuant to revisions and updates to the continuity of operations plan promulgated to the Manager and the University.
Manager’s point of contact (or reasonable temporary substitutions therefor) shall be available twenty-four (24) hours, seven (7) days a week.
The provision of security services and implementation of other security measures by the Manager hereunder is not guaranteed to deter criminal activity, and neither Lessee nor Manager shall be liable to the other or any other Person by reason of the criminal activities of any third party.
Section 8.3 Cooperation with University for Residence Life Services .

The Manager shall not be responsible for establishing, implementing, administering and/or managing various living-learning, social, educational, student conduct and crisis management activities and programs at the Student Housing Facilities (each, a “Residence Life Program”) for any of the Residents.
The Lessee and the Manager shall cooperate at all times with the University for the seamless and orderly performance of their respective responsibilities under the Transaction Documents to ensure the Student Housing Facilities are appropriately integrated into the Campus and to allow the University to provide a Residence Life Program for the Residents.
Section 8.4 Employment of Personnel .
Subject to the requirements of the Transaction Documents, the Manager shall hire, pay, supervise and discharge, as appropriate, all employees, contractors, subcontractors or others necessary for the performance of its obligations under this Agreement.
All such personnel shall be the employees or independent contractors of the Manager and not of the Lessee.

All matters pertaining to the employment of such employees or engagement of such independent contractors shall be the sole responsibility of the Manager, and the Lessee shall bear absolutely no responsibility or liability therefor.
The Manager shall fully comply with all Applicable Laws concerning worker’s

15 4923-6384-1828.6 compensation, social security, unemployment, tax w ithholding and reporting, hours of labor, wages, working conditions and all other Applicable Laws affecting or respecting the employment of such employees or the engagement of such independent contractors.
The Manager shall have no authority to enter into any employment contract that purports to be on behalf of the Lessee, or that otherwise obligates the Lessee in any respect.
The Lessee reserves the right from time to time and at any time to require that employees or independent contractors performing any services relating to the Student Housing Facilities be subject to a satisfactory background or security check performed by the Lessee or, at the Lessee’s election, by the Manager.
All costs of such background or security checks shall be Program Expenses.
